MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 10, 2026
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on February 10, 2026, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 5, 2026, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez (arrived 5:10pm)
  Mayor Bucknum
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  John R. Harper, Interim City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

 CLOSED SESSION

 CS1.  Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Property Los Osos, 25282 Marguerite
  Parkway: Agency Negotiators; Elaine Lister, City Manager, Jerry Hill, Assistant City
  Manager, and John Harper, Interim City Attorney: Negotiating Party: Santa
  Margarita Water District General Manager: Under Negotiation: Price and Terms

 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

 At the hour of 5:01pm Mayor Bucknum recessed to Closed Session. At the hour of 6:01pm Mayor
 Bucknum reconvened the meeting with all five Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  February 10, 2026
  REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

 Interim City Attorney Harper announced there was no reportable action on item CS1.

 INVOCATION: Council Member Ruesch

 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

 PRESENTATIONS

 P1.  Recognize the 2025 Employees of the Year

  Mayor Bucknum presented certificates of commendation to (1) Animal Control Officer
  Stephanie DeAlmeida, City of Mission Viejo Employee of the Year; (2) Fire Apparatus
  Engineer, and Paramedic Max Harter, Orange County Fire Authority Employee of the Year;
  and (3) Deputy Cameron Mosher, Orange County Sheriff’s Department Employee of the
  Year.

 P2.  Proclaim the Month of February 2026 To Be American Heart Month

  Mayor Bucknum presented proclamation.

 PUBLIC COMMENTS

 Michael Rotcher, M.V.: Stated former Mayor/Council Member Raths’ claim that he was yelled
 at during a protest is false. He called attempts to link Council Member Cynthia Vasquez to the
 group “revenge politics” and defended the group’s actions as peaceful, democratic expression.

 Sophia Borazjani, M.V.: Spoke on the Community Character Trait of the Month Unity. She
 highlighted its importance and gave examples of the trait Unity.

 Shirley Bates, M.V.: Shared photos of neighbor’s behavior at 26531 Mimosa, (PODs, trash
 cans, and frequent trucks) claiming repeated violations for the past 2–3 years that impact nearby
 disabled neighbors and asked for the City’s help.

 Peggy O’Neill, M.V.: Urged the Council to invite the Orange County Registrar of Voters to
 hold a community presentation to explain election procedures, security, and checks and
 balances, and to answer questions to counter misinformation and restore public trust.

 Jim Farris, M.V.: Provided a handout requesting the Council commission an independent
 operational and financial review of the City and raised concerns about rising crime, perceived
 police inaction, and code-enforcement issues.

 Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Thanked staff for recent handicapped parking fixes and urged proactive
 accessibility improvements. He also accused the Council of sidelining a non-white member
City Council Minutes  2  February 10, 2026
  drawing parallels to federal removals of Black officials and urged the Council to stop racist
 actions.

 Steve Thornton, M.V.: A Wilderness Glen resident thanked the Council and staff for
 fuel-reduction work that protects homes and reduces wildfire risk. He urged continued pursuit
 of grants and praised the Crucero Park renovations.

 Carolyn Gatto, M.V.: Disputed Greg Raths’ January 27, claim that protesters at La Paz and
 Marguerite harassed him, saying she did not hear any disparagement of his military service or
 anyone asking him to leave. She also condemned his personal and inappropriate attack on
 Council Member Cynthia Vasquez and urged speakers to refrain from airing personal grudges.

 Tom Moore, M.V.: Provided a handout about the obelisk and urged the Council to continue
 clearing overgrown vegetation at the San Felipe “knuckle” to improve visibility and access to
 the Oso Creek corridor and the planned obelisk.

 Barbara Casserly, M.V.: Stated residents are not being heard. She criticized the Council’s
 budget choices, the sidelining of Council Member Cynthia Vasquez, faulted their silence on a
 racist school board incident, objected to praise for a speaker who attacked Council Member
 Cynthia Vasquez and urged the Council to listen, be more responsive and respectful.

 Len Pastick, M.V.: Praised the City Council’s work but argued Council Member Cynthia
 Vasquez was unfairly passed over for Mayor or Mayor Pro Tem despite strong public support
 and qualifications. He urged voters to choose inclusive Council Members in the 2026 election
 and encouraged Council Member Vasquez to run for re-election.

 CONSENT CALENDAR

 Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to approve the
 Consent Calendar outlined below.

 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

 AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
 NOES:  None
 ABSENT:  None

 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of January 27, 2026, as presented.

 2.  General Check Register dated January 16, 2026, in the amount of $1,371,117.47

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  February 10, 2026
  3.  General Check Register Dated January 23, 2026, in the Amount of $1,298,402.13

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 4.  Golf Check Register Dated January 16, 2026, in the Amount of $200,702.09

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 5.  Golf Check Register Dated January 23, 2026, in the Amount of $20,021.96

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December 2025

  Received and filed.

 7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for December 2025

  Received and filed.

 8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for December 2025

  Received and filed.

 9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December
  2025

  Received and filed.

 10.  Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Report for the quarter ending December 31, 2025

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Report for the quarter ending
  December 31, 2025.

 11.  Memorandum of Understanding between City of Mission Viejo and Pacific Symphony

  Approved Memorandum of Understanding between City of Mission Viejo and Pacific
  Symphony for FY 26/27 programs amounting to $116,000.

 13.  Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Adopt Resolution 26-03 Providing for the Revisions to Select Personnel Policies.

City Council Minutes  4  February 10, 2026
  ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

 12.  City of Mission Viejo Safe Routes to School Action Plan Project (CIP 26269)

  Transportation Engineer Mario Gutierrez presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to award a
  contract to CR Associates (CRA) (A26-03) in an amount not to exceed $559,689.00 for
  transportation engineering services for the subject project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 NEW BUSINESS

 14.  2026 Orange County Multisport Festival in Mission Viejo

  Director of Public Works Rich Schlesinger presented the staff report.

  Micheala Watson, Villa Park; Christina Vaughan, Orange; and Russ Jones, San Juan
  Capistrano: Spoke in favor of this event.

  Motion made by Council Member Ruesch, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to (1)
  approve the request submitted by Five Point Events to hold the 2026 Orange County
  Multisport Festival in Mission Viejo on Sunday, April 26, 2026.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ruesch, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to approve
  the request for City in-kind funding to Five Point Events matching contributions not to exceed
  $15,000 for the 2026 Orange County Multisport Festival as described in Exhibit D and
  provide direction to City staff.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Ruesch
  NOES:  Vasquez
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  5  February 10, 2026
  15.  Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2025/26

  Director of Administrative Services Ellis Chang presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to adopt
  Resolution 26-04 Amending the FY 2025/26 Budget for Adjustments to Certain Revenue
  Sources and Operating and Capital Improvement Program Appropriations.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Council members provided input.

 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

 16.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Received written report.

 CITY MANAGER REPORTS

 City Manager Lister reported that a previously delayed grant through Congresswoman Young Kim’s
 Office was approved by Congress about a week ago and the city is awaiting contact from the awarding
 agency. She also provided a brief update on the RFQ for legal services, stating staff received six
 responses which they are reviewing and will forward the selected firms to the ad hoc committee, and
 will schedule a Special Council meeting (date TBD) for final interviews and selection.

 CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

 No report given.

 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

 17.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

City Council Minutes  6  February 10, 2026
  Council Member Kelley

 Council Member Kelley congratulated the Employees of the Year and thanked them for their service.
 She attended the successful grand reopening of Crucero Park and encouraged residents to visit. She
 also reminded the community of the upcoming Oso Fit event on Saturday, February 28, and recognized
 Community of Character Committee student Sophia Borazjani for her consistent participation in
 meetings and city events.

 Council Member Ruesch

 Council Member Ruesch announced he participated in an OC Focus interview and gave an OCFA
 update; stating the search for a new permanent fire chief is underway with TJ McGovern serving as
 interim; the equipment-replacement program keeps roughly 55 additional units available to avoid
 shortages; like those in the Palisades fire. He also shared the recent completion of Station 24, that
 Station 9 (near the mall) is prioritized for replacement in the next 3–4 years, and Station 31 will be
 evaluated for repairs and upgrades.

 Council Member Vasquez

 18.  Community Education and Resources for Mission Viejo Residents, Workers & Visitors

  Council Member Vasquez presented her report.

  Michael Rotcher, M.V.; Laycee Barragato, M.V.; Cathy Palmer, M.V.; Annie Cwieka, M.V.;
  and Barbara Casserly, M.V.; Spoke in support of Council Member Vasquez’s recommended
  resource list.

  Dale Tyler, M.V.: Urged the City not to provide resources that could help undocumented
  immigrants evade enforcement, called for support of law-abiding residents who feel fearful,
  and insisted the City uphold and enforce immigration laws.

  Council members provided input.

  Motion made by Council Member Vasquez, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to direct
  staff to compile a list of resources to help educate residents, workers, and visitors about recent
  immigration enforcement actions in Orange County, adding concrete “what not to do”
  guidance and preventative tips from law enforcement, language encouraging non-interference
  with law enforcement and adherence to the law, carefully vetting links (noting ICE.org as a
  comprehensive source) and recommended staff return with a proposed vetted list and
  suggested wording at the February 24, 2026, Council meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  7  February 10, 2026
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

 Mayor Pro Tem stated he was glad to be back after several business trips that caused recent absences,
 including attending a film festival in Palermo where a documentary he was a part of about an event
 from 50 years ago received recognition. He noted he and his wife enjoyed the trip and concluded by
 saying he expects to be present and engaged in Council meetings for the next few months.

 Mayor Bucknum

 Mayor Bucknum thanked Commissioner Steve Thorton for the Crucero Park grand opening. Shared
 she did a promotional segment on American Dream TV about people moving to and staying in Mission
 Viejo. Stated she will share the Registrar of Voters presentation date, once scheduled. Mentioned she
 attended the Galentine’s Book Authors Club hosted by the library and reminded residents of the Oso
 Fit event on Saturday, February 28, and pickleball/tennis tournaments the first weekend in March at
 Felipe and Marguerite Tennis Recreation Centers. She concluded by asking staff to place an item on
 the next agenda to discuss plans for a committee’s proposal for an America’s 250th Birthday Parade.

ADJOURNMENT

 At the hour of 8:32 pm, with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
 Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, February 24, 2026, at 5:00 p.m.

 ______________________________________
 Renata Winter
 Assistant City Clerk

City Council Minutes  8  February 10, 2026
